checks: The two families of balanced sign columns have the stated count, and the unchanged last coordinate forces any dependence to have zero sum of coefficients. Coordinates in the two families then eliminate every difference coefficient. The resulting row relation is unique and strictly positive. Independent rational rank checks for odd dimensions 3 through 23 agree with the proof.

The barycentric formulas give exactly the d+2 sampled bases. The exposing forms take d on their own outer vertex, −1 on each other outer vertex, and zero centrally. The outer cube coupling sums to the ambient zero vector with uniform marginals, so it pays at least V for every through-cap. Exposing tilts give the matching central upper bound and the strictly smaller outer depth bounds.

The chosen margins strictly allocate one whole outer cube and half the central cube. Dividing by √d normalizes all continuous normals with equal scale. The sections are proper and central, with a common positive area and zero first moments by cube symmetries.

The finite cube facets have unique owner except on lower-dimensional boundaries. A selected cap's boundary has facet-area-null intersection with a central facet since it depends on every free coordinate there. Hence its true trace equals the indicator almost everywhere.

On any central facet, symmetry of the sum of the free signed coordinates and balanced fixed-coordinate signs give N/2 facet areas. Reflection, zero mean and atomlessness give equality of the transverse coordinate integrals at the two thresholds ±1 before multiplying by the row sign. Column balance cancels each transverse aggregate first moment. The fixed coordinate and outer traces give exactly the objective moment vector after multiplication by λ.

The assigned group's single coverage multiplier t=NλS supplies λS=ρt, and its assigned base and all section first moments are zero, so the cap-side base and continuous moment equations hold. Slack outer groups have zero multipliers. The projected cover constraint at the deepest base binds. Scaling to central volume one preserves these equalities.
The exact Euler sum is 2(d+2)/3=1/β. For d≥3 it exceeds 3, while (1+1/d)^d<e<3. The d=3 subtraction gives 26/27, also verified by rational arithmetic.

overlap.comparison: The accepted theorem states the moment identities at a minimizer. The draft realizes those identities for a particular selected cover on an actual example and compares its multiplier sum. It does not invoke minimizer stationarity.

The existing tetrahedron-product counterexample has rank three in ambient continuous dimension D≥4. The present independent cube geometry has full continuous rank in every odd d≥3 and uses different exact depth, section and facet data.

readability: The shared freely moving planes are the 2d cube planes. The base simplex is fixed. The proof claims uniqueness of the deepest base, without needing uniqueness of its maximizing mark.
